title: Equality-free intuitionistic first-order sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Build equality-free constructive first-order sequent trees with protected parameters, structural operations and exact native-deduction translations through explicit cuts.
abstract: A proof about every object must leave its chosen parameter arbitrary, while a proof that an object exists may use a particular witness. We add these two kinds of step to constructive sequents with one conclusion. Their finite proof trees can be weakened, renamed and substituted without disturbing the fresh parameters. They give intuitionistic natural deductions without equality rules; conversely, such a deduction with equality-free assumptions and conclusion gives a sequent tree when explicit composition steps are allowed. A separate treatment of temporary names explains how a constant-free language can have a public existential proof while having no raw proof over an empty supply of terms.
